The '''R2n Agromech Head''' was a model of [[agromech droid]] head manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]].<ref name="DroidWorks" /> Often described as an inverted flowerpot, it was less graceful in appearance than the [[R2a Astromech Head]]<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide">''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''</ref> and a row of three tiny [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] and [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] replaced the large [[Radar/Legends|radar]] eye found on earlier models. The R2n featured an [[Audio sensor/Legends|auditory sensor]], [[Broadband antenna/Legends|broadband antenna/receiver]], [[Electromagnetic field receptor|electromagnetic field sensor unit]], [[Holoprojector/Legends|holographic projector]], and [[Infrared receptor|infrared sensor]].<ref name="TEGtD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> It weighed 33 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]], was made from [[Copper/Legends|copper]], [[Plastic/Legends|plastic]], and [[silicon carbide]], and was [[Magnet/Legends|magnetic]].<ref name="DroidWorks" /> The R2n was incorporated into the [[R5-series astromech droid]], and existing R2n heads were reused in Industrial Automaton's line of [[R2-AG agromech droid|R2-AG]] and [[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4]] agromechs to recoup losses following the R5's discontinuation.<ref name="IA Pulls R5's Plug">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|business/13228_3.html|IA Pulls R5's Plug}}</ref>

Some [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] disliked the R2n on their [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Astromech socket/Legends|counterparts]], as it offered a larger target profile to enemy [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]].<ref name="TEGtD" />

{{Tech-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The R2n Agromech Head was first identified in ''[[Star Wars: DroidWorks]]'', a [[1998]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Wikipedia:Educational entertainment|educational]] video game developed and published by [[Lucas Learning]] for [[Wikipedia:Personal computer|PC]] and [[Wikipedia:Mac (computer)|Mac]].<ref name="DroidWorks" />
